title: Dedicated supply-chain provisioning, authorization, and run-rate planner
creator: Liam Ortega
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines the end-to-end "supply-chain" for dedicated capacity requests: intake signals, authorization (approval matrix and SLA alignment), run-rate planning (forecast -> reservation sizing -> cadence), and the orchestration controls that tie autoscaling and fleet guardrails to approved reservations.

Goals:
- Create a deterministic provisioning flow that maps business requests to reserved throughput guarantees and autoscale policies.
- Reduce manual triage surface by 60% for medium/large requests via an automated eligibility scorer and default sizing heuristics.
- Ensure every approved reservation publishes a canonical run-rate (QPS/Tokens/min), cost estimate, and rollback policy visible in Console and billing exports.

Scope / Out of scope:
In scope: intake form schema, approval matrix rules, default sizing heuristics, approval ticket automation, Console intake UX, cost/run-rate estimator, audit trail & webhooks for downstream fleets.
Out of scope: full fleet scheduler rearchitecture, new pricing tiers (handled by finance follow-up).

User stories:
- As a Platform Engineer, I want a single intake that captures workload signal (p95 latency target, request distribution, token profile), so the provisioning team can size capacity without multiple clarifying loops.
- As a Product Owner, I want to see an estimated monthly bill and committed throughput for approved reservations before signoff.
- As an Oncall, I want the approval to automatically create a scoped escalation policy and a canary window tied to the reservation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form (API + Console) accepts structured workload signals and provides a nonbinding estimate within 24 hours.
- Approval matrix implementation supports at least three tiers (self-serve, delegated, executive) mapped to budget and SLO bands.
- Approved reservation produces a machine-readable contract (reservation id, run_rate, autoscale_policy_id, fallback_model_variant) and a human-friendly summary in Console.
- Console shows run-rate, projected cost, linked playbook, and a one-click revoke/scale-down action.
- Audit log and KMS-tagged keys present for every approval event.

Design/implementation notes:
- Use a scoring heuristic combining historical usage (when available), declared burst profile, and a percentile-based safety buffer. Keep heuristic tunable via feature flags.
- Autoscale policy primitives: min_reservation, target_utilization (e.g., 70% GPU), burst_credit, cooldown_seconds. Map these to fleet controls in Dedicated runtime.
- Fallback plan: when capacity not available, route to compatible cheaper model variant with a per-request option to accept cost-quality tradeoff.
- Billing projection: integrate with cost model microservice to return committed vs on-demand split and a 12-month runway.

API / Console contracts:
- POST /reservations/intake -> returns intake_id, preliminary_score, estimated_run_rate, estimated_monthly_cost.
- POST /reservations/{intake_id}/request-approval -> triggers approval workflow, returns approval_id and required approvers.
- GET /reservations/{reservation_id} -> returns reservation contract: [reservation_id, run_rate, autoscale_policy_id, fleet_scope, approved_by, start_date, end_date, billing_estimate_url].

Operational runbook highlights:
- Canary: default 48-hour canary with an auto-rollback if error rate >2x baseline or latency SLA breached.
- Escalation: tie reservation alerts to oncall team with playbook link.
- Decommission: support decommit windows and credit reclamation for short-lived test reservations.

Metrics / success signals:
- Time from intake to approval (target median < 2 business days).
- % of requests that require clarifying questions (target < 25%).
- Reservation utilization vs committed run-rate (target average utilization 65–85%).
- Number of production incidents attributable to mis-sized reservations (target < 2 per quarter).

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal Platform team only – validate intake schema and estimator (2 weeks).
2) Beta: select enterprise customers and Redwood partners (4 weeks).
3) GA: public for all Dedicated customers with Console and API support (8 weeks), paired with support runbook and billing export.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: estimator under-sizes high variance workloads -> Mitigation: conservative safety buffer, mandatory canary, allow rapid temporary bump.
- Risk: approval matrix too rigid -> Mitigation: create delegated approver roles and override path with audit trail.
- Risk: operator confusion about autoscale primitives -> Mitigation: provide default policy templates and in-Console recommendations.

Open questions:
- What SLA tiers should map to which approval lanes for 3rd-party compliance customers? (security/compliance to advise)
- Should we support multi-region reservations at launch or ship region-scoped first? (X-Region increases complexity for run-rate guarantees)

Next steps / deliverables:
- Finalize intake schema in Confluence and publish Console mocks (DES task).
- Implement scorer prototype (ENG task) and expose a /estimate endpoint for early testing.
- Draft approval matrix and delegated roles with Legal and Security.
- Create end-to-end test plan for canary and rollback scenarios.
